description: What the library promises when something goes wrong part way through, for each fault point of the recovery runner (design section 7.1). It was written by reading the code and its doc comments, not by running anything, so that the runner tests a contract and does not guess one. `contract` is nothing_committed (the state afterwards is the state before), partly_committed (a documented part of the change is kept and a defined retry puts the rest right), or undocumented. An undocumented point is not tested against a guess: the runner records what it sees and reports it as a finding. A point stays in this table when it is fixed, with the contract it now has. `public` means the promise is in a public doc comment, and `code` that it is in the comment of an item that is not public.

points.operation: Scene::add_node
points.says: A failure at any step between creating an element and finishing the node removes every element it made, so nothing is left rendered, and the model is only changed after the element is attached.

points.operation: Scene::move_node, the write of the node's transform
points.says: If the node's transform cannot be written, the call returns an error and the node is exactly where it was, in the model and on the page. node_rect never describes a position that was not drawn.

points.operation: Scene::move_node, the redraw of the incident connectors
points.says: Once the transform has been written the move is committed and is not rolled back. If a connector then fails to update, the call returns an error, the node stays moved, node_rect reports the new position, and some incident connectors can be redrawn and others not.
points.retry: The next move of the node, or of a node at the other end of one of its edges, to a different origin recomputes every incident connector.

points.operation: Scene::move_node, the placing of edge labels
points.says: If an edge label fails to update after the transform was written, the call returns an error, the node stays moved, and the label is marked as having missed the move.
points.retry: A move_node to the origin the node already has redraws no connector, and retries the label that failed to place.

points.operation: Scene::make_draggable_with
points.says: If set_attr or any one of the four pointer-listener registrations fails part way, the node is left exactly as it was, is not marked draggable, and none of the method's listeners are left on it. A failed call can safely be retried.

points.operation: Scene::add_edge_with
points.says: Adding an edge is a transaction. If any write fails (making the connector's path, putting it in the scene, styling it, or naming either end), the call returns the error and the scene is exactly as it was: no path is left behind, neither node's name has the new relationship in it, and the edge is not in the graph. The edge is recorded last, after everything that can fail. This was not so before 0.2.48: the sweep of this point found that a failure after the path was attached left a stray path, and that a retry then added a second.

points.operation: A view change written in an animation frame
points.says: A wheel or pan event updates the view at once and leaves the DOM write to the next frame. A frame callback has nowhere to report an error, and a failed write leaves the view marked as waiting. If the browser refuses the request for a frame, nothing is pending, so the next call tries again.
points.retry: The next wheel or pan event requests a frame again, and the write catches the DOM up to the latest view.

points.operation: Dropping the last Scene handle with a view write pending
points.says: A pending frame is cancelled before its closure goes, so the browser never calls a dropped function. A view change that has not reached the DOM is written when the scene is dropped, so the graph is drawn as the last input left it. The scene's listeners are released with it. The DOM it drew stays until the host is removed. After the host is removed the page is as it was before the scene.

points.operation: Dropping the last Scene handle between a pointer down and a pointer up
points.says: The pointer handlers hold only weak references to the scene and upgrade them when they run, so once the scene is gone a handler that runs finds nothing and returns. After the host is removed the page is as it was before the scene. The grabbing cursor is taken off the dragged node when the scene is dropped, because the pointer-down handler owns a guard that puts the idle style back as it is released. The node's <g> stays in the document for as long as the host does.

points.operation: Removing the host <svg> from the document while the Scene is alive, and then using the Scene
points.says: The documentation of `Scene` (section "Keep the host <svg> in the document") says that a scene is supported only while its host is in the document, and that nothing is guaranteed for an operation made while it is not. What was observed is not a promise: five operations succeeded, and the scene agreed with the model when the host was put back. Operations that measure are not covered. So this stays a finding and is not judged as a contract.

points.operation: Surface::build, which draws the scene, the overlay and the reserved data node
points.says: A failure at any DOM call while the surface is built returns the error and makes no surface, so no Surface exists to draw on. The scene's own add_data_node draws a node as a transaction, so a failure there leaves the scene as it was. The caller removes the host and builds again on a fresh one. A failure in the first draw of the controller that is built on it is a draw like any other, and belongs to the overlay and the setter.
points.retry: Building again on a fresh host.

points.operation: Scene::set_data_values on the reserved data node, which every draw makes
points.says: A failure part way through the cells leaves some cells rewritten and the node's values as they were, and marks the node. The next call, whatever values it asks for, writes every cell, changed or not, and clears the mark when it has written them all. Until finding F1 of the S0 audit was closed, a call that asked for the values the node still held changed nothing and left the node torn.
points.retry: One call to Scene::set_data_values with the last committed values. The controller's repair is that call, as part of the full redraw.

points.operation: The draw of a slice, which writes the fields of the overlay and then the data node
points.says: A write that fails leaves the page partly written. No new slice is committed, the cursor and the model are as they were, playback is stopped, the page is marked dirty and one failure is reported. The controller then makes one immediate full redraw of the committed slice, and if that fails the page stays dirty and stopped.
points.retry: Repair, which draws the committed slice again in full, and then the slice again.

points.operation: The writes of the Play control's ARIA state and label, which Play and Pause make
points.says: A write of the control that fails leaves it half written and the page says nothing: the cursor is where it was, and playback is as the controller says. The host remembers that the control is stale, and a full draw writes its content and ARIA again from what the controller last said. A repair never starts or stops playback.
points.retry: Repair, which writes the control again.

points.operation: The request for the timer that the next slice of playback waits for
points.says: If the page refuses a timer the callback does not exist, so nothing is committed. The last committed display stays, playback stops, and one failure is reported. The next timer is asked for only after a slice was committed.
points.retry: Play, which asks for the timer again.

points.operation: The request for the animation frame that a seek replays at
points.says: If the page refuses a frame the seek is not started and nothing is committed. The cursor stays, the target is kept as the retry, one failure is reported, and no synchronous replay is made in its place.
points.retry: Retry, which asks for the frame again.

points.operation: A gallery panel that holds the host is hidden, with the hint that the page gives and without it
points.says: Hiding stops playback, takes back what was scheduled, and moves the epoch and the seek token, so a callback that was already on its way is stale. It is not promised that no callback runs while the panel is hidden. It is promised that one that does is inert: it commits nothing and writes nothing. Showing the panel again repairs a dirty page and never resumes playback.
points.retry: Play, which a person presses after the panel is shown.

points.operation: A draw that is asked for while the host is out of the document
points.says: A detached element accepts writes without complaint, so the host is checked and not discovered: the surface refuses a detached host before any write, and the controller does not draw. Nothing is written and nothing is committed. On return the committed slice is drawn again in full, and the cursor does not advance.
points.retry: Presence, which is told when the host returns, and then the slice again.

points.operation: A draw whose host leaves the document after any of its writes
points.says: A write that went through is no evidence that the page is attached, so the guard is asked again after the draw. A host that left in the middle of it leaves the page partly written, and the slice is not committed: the cursor and the model are as they were, playback is stopped, the page is marked dirty and the host is announced as unavailable once.
points.retry: Presence, told when the host returns, which draws the committed slice again in full.

points.operation: A timer or frame callback that runs after the controller was disposed
points.says: Disposing marks the controller first, then takes back what it scheduled, so a callback that was already on its way finds the controller disposed or its token moved and does nothing: no slice is committed, no DOM is written and no notice is changed. It holds only a weak reference, so nothing is kept alive, and no closure or listener is left.
points.retry: None: a disposed controller is never resumed.
